geo.label: Myanmar military seized power (February 2021)
geo.text: The Myanmar military seized power on 1 February 2021. A civil war has followed between the military and ethnic armed organisations and anti-regime militias.

geo.label: Junta-run election and presidency (December 2025 to April 2026)
geo.text: The military junta held a multistage general election from 28 December 2025 into January 2026, the first since the 2021 coup. The UN Special Rapporteur on Myanmar called it neither free nor fair. The military-backed USDP won. Min Aung Hlaing stepped down as commander-in-chief in March 2026 and was elected president on 3 April 2026.
geo.source: Britannica; Wikipedia (2026 Myanmar presidential election); UN Special Rapporteur (as reported)

milops.label: Armed groups hold large parts of Myanmar (Chatham House, January 2026)
milops.text: A Chatham House analysis estimates that ethnic armed organisations and anti-regime militias control around 38 per cent of the country. It also reports that the military retook 26 bases and camps it had lost in 2025. The figures are analytical estimates, not official data.

milops.label: China announces junta-MNDAA ceasefire (January 2025)
milops.text: On 20 January 2025 China announced that it had brokered a ceasefire between the junta and the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA), as reported in Wikipedia's record of 2025 events in Myanmar.

milops.label: Thailand-Cambodia border clashes and ceasefire (July 2025 to May 2026)
milops.text: Armed clashes between Thai and Cambodian forces began on 24 July 2025 and displaced more than 200,000 people. A ceasefire was agreed on 27 December 2025. It remained in effect as of May 2026, with sporadic incidents and deep mistrust.
milops.source: Wikipedia: 2025 Cambodian-Thai border crisis (citing Thai PBS and others)

mss.label: Thailand cut power to Myanmar border towns hosting scam operations (February 2025)
mss.text: On 5 February 2025 Thailand stopped supplying electricity to several Myanmar border towns that are known to host scam operations.

econ.label: China-Laos railway opened (December 2021)
econ.text: The China-Laos railway, linking Kunming with Vientiane through the border station at Boten, opened in December 2021.

scs.label: Strait of Malacca: a critical chokepoint (EIA)
scs.text: The Strait of Malacca is one of the world's busiest shipping lanes and a critical route for energy bound for China, according to the US Energy Information Administration.

scs.label: Bangladesh-Myanmar maritime boundary settled by the ICJ (March 2012)
scs.text: The International Court of Justice drew the maritime boundary between Bangladesh and Myanmar in the Bay of Bengal in its March 2012 judgment, settling a dispute that had run since 2008.

wellbeing.label: World Happiness Report 2026: Myanmar's rank not verified
wellbeing.text: The 2026 World Happiness Report ranks for Myanmar and the region around it were not verified in this build. Check the report directly.
wellbeing.source: World Happiness Report 2026 (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Naypyidaw
markers.note: Capital of Myanmar; seat of the military government since 2005.

markers.name: Yangon
markers.note: Myanmar's largest city and main commercial port.

markers.name: Mandalay
markers.note: Second city and former royal capital.

markers.name: Mawlamyine (Mon State)
markers.note: Capital of Mon State, on the Gulf of Martaban.

markers.name: Defence Services (Tatmadaw) headquarters, Naypyidaw
markers.note: Seat of the military government. The military seized power on 1 February 2021. Location approximate.

markers.name: Mingaladon Air Base (Yangon)
markers.note: Myanmar Air Force base beside Yangon International Airport (public information). Location approximate.

markers.name: Sittwe (Rakhine State)
markers.note: Rakhine State capital. The Arakan Army contests control of much of the state (press reporting). Front lines change; verify the latest situation.

markers.name: Myitkyina (Kachin State)
markers.note: Kachin State capital. Fighting between the Kachin Independence Army and the military has been reported around the city (press reporting).

markers.name: Laiza (Kachin Independence Army headquarters)
markers.note: Headquarters of the Kachin Independence Army, on the China border (press reporting). Location approximate.

markers.name: Lashio (northern Shan State)
markers.note: Northern Shan State town. Control has changed hands in 2024 and 2025 (press reporting). Verify the latest situation. Location approximate.

markers.name: Myawaddy (Thai-Myanmar border)
markers.note: Border town where scam compounds have been reported (press reporting). Thailand cut power to border towns hosting such operations in February 2025.

markers.name: Coco Islands (Myanmar)
markers.note: Reports of Chinese electronic listening facilities on these islands are press-reported and not officially confirmed by Myanmar or China.

markers.name: Kyaukphyu deep-sea port and pipeline terminus
markers.note: China-backed deep-sea port in Rakhine State, reported as the terminus of the China-Myanmar oil and gas pipelines. Status and terms are reported, not independently verified.

markers.name: China-Myanmar gas pipeline, Muse crossing
markers.note: Gas pipeline route from the China border at Muse towards Mandalay and Yangon (press reporting). Location approximate.

markers.name: Thilawa port and special economic zone
markers.note: Port and special economic zone south of Yangon (public information). Location approximate.

markers.name: Dawei deep-sea port project
markers.note: Deep-sea port and industrial zone project on the Andaman coast, announced with Thai backing (press reporting). Status not verified.

markers.name: Coco Channel (Andaman Islands to Coco Islands)
markers.note: Channel between the Andaman Islands and Myanmar's Coco Islands, cited in strategic reporting. Location approximate.
